claims.statement: Unit tests never touch a database: conftest.make_app builds a router-only FastAPI app with no lifespan and overrides get_current_user, get_principal and get_pool, where get_pool returns a _SentinelPool that raises AssertionError on any attribute access, so tests must monkeypatch repository functions; an autouse fixture also removes STORAGE_BUCKET_SUFFIX from the environment so a developer's shell cannot rename the buckets tests expect.

Integration tests connect to TEST_DATABASE_URL (default compose Postgres on localhost:5433), skip rather than fail when the database is unreachable, and isolate by rolling back; the integration marker is registered in pyproject and applied per file or per test, and pytest -m "not integration" excludes them.

Evals are gated by a --run-evals conftest flag, not an addopts -m filter: without the flag every test with the eval keyword is skipped, because a command-line -m would replace an addopts -m and could otherwise start billing model calls; evals also skip when the provider API key for the configured model is missing or Postgres is unreachable, and their database connections are read-only so they can safely target staging.

make evals runs pytest tests/evals --run-evals on the host venv (not in the container, which lacks pytest) after sourcing .env quietly in an @-prefixed recipe, with TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at localhost:5433 (or the managed database under ENV=staging); TAG maps to --eval-tag and K to -k; it sets Langfuse eval environment and release variables; it costs real money (about 10 cents per case, and about $0.90 for the cost case that a run with no TAG includes).

Ask evals load cases from cases/*.jsonl and run the real agent as the staff dev user with an in-memory checkpointer, a recursion limit of 60 and a 180-second default timeout (a case may override it with timeout_seconds); they extract executed SQL (db_query 'executed:' lines) and [kind:id] citation markers from the final answer, skipping the audit caveat message, and score against gold SQL results, expected values, required/forbidden citations, mention rules, must_decline and per-tool call budgets; cases with expected_failure are strict xfail so a fixed data bug shows as XPASS failure.

Import evals only run when --eval-tag matches a case, so a bare make evals stays the cheap Ask suite; the two canary cases (a funder and an NGO) carry both import and canary tags and need a Tavily key (TAVILY_API_KEY or settings.tavily_api_key). run_import runs the real Import agent as staff with a 900-second timeout, answers the choose_sources pause with web plus library and raises on any other pause, and the test judges the saved entity_research row (kind, findings, expected concepts, gap reasons, tag_note, summary fact_count) plus per-case max_calls tool-call budgets.

test_harness.py pins the agent tool surfaces: the deepagents general-purpose subagent is disabled and the profile does not decide tools; the replacement FilesystemMiddleware exposes only read_file (or read_file and ls); Ask Sangam has no task tool and exactly eight tools (db_list_tables, db_describe_table, db_profile_column, db_query, search_graph, compare_fit, read_file, ls) with no fetch_url; neither agent has write_file, edit_file, delete, execute, glob or grep; Import's task description lists entity-researcher and catalog-writer and not general-purpose (the test checks those entries, not an exact set; the exact four compiled subagents are asserted separately).

test_harness.py pins each compiled Import subagent's own tool list by inspecting the task tool's closure: entity-researcher, catalog-writer and vault-reader have fixed sets, none has ls, none can write files or execute, the vault reader has no web tools, and after read_source_rows is used the researcher's read_page is refused (STAFF_LOCK_REPLY).

Import model tiers and skills are pinned: subagents run on strong/mid/cheap tiers with fallback to the next tier, blank model variables take defaults and 'off' disables sql_audit_model, skills live in app/ingest/skills one directory deep with name matching directory and a 'use when' description, and the supervisor and researcher skill names are pinned as literal sets.

The SQL catalog is treated as a security control: tests assert withheld tables (checkpoints, users, threads, schema_migrations, graph_ingest_log) and columns (contacts email/phone, chunks embedding) are absent including from SELECT * expansion, citation kinds stay within org/funder/activity/score/news, and the import-time self-check rejects a dangling foreign key.

test_sql_validator.py pins what the SQL validator must refuse: non-SELECT statements, writes hidden in CTEs, SELECT INTO, locking clauses, multiple statements, withheld or unknown tables (including in CTEs and union arms), cross-schema references, CTEs shadowing real tables and dangerous functions; it runs without a database.

The catalog is checked against the live schema: test_no_drift fails if a catalogued table or column is missing from Postgres, and every live base table must be catalogued or in KNOWN_EXCLUDED, so a migration adding a table forces an explicit decision.

test_sql_integration.py proves server-side guards independent of the validator: read-only transactions refuse writes, statement_timeout cancels runaway queries, neither setting leaks onto the pooled connection shared with the LangGraph checkpointer, prepare=True is required to refuse multi-statement input, and executor concurrency stays below the pool size.

test_prompt.py keeps the Ask system prompt consistent with code: every citation marker kind emitted by tools or CITE_COLUMNS appears in SYSTEM_PROMPT, every registered tool name is mentioned, the prompt's retry budget equals MAX_SQL_ATTEMPTS (in app/ask/middleware.py), and the prompt's table map lists every catalog table with its description.

test_rls.py pins row-level security against live Postgres by building orgs, roles and private rows in a rolled-back transaction and querying as each caller via role and request.jwt.claims settings (as CallerPool does): private rows reach only the owning org and staff, hidden orgs only staff, anonymous callers cannot use org-private tables, threads reach only owner and staff, and membership rules (last admin, one org per admin/member) hold.

test_caller_pool.py pins that requests run as anon or authenticated with the token subject claim, that connections return to the pool as the owner with claims cleared, and that InsufficientPrivilege maps to a 403 with detail 'Not allowed'.

Migration and seed integrity is tested by test_migration_integrity.py against the live database (preserved documents and graph_ingest_log counts, stable seed-order ids, advanced documents sequence, v2 content), and make up migrates before starting the backend because _verify_sql_catalog raises when a catalogued table is missing.

Proposal editing is enforced in the database as well as in Python: test_rls.py shows a proposal reaches only its org and staff, only admins, stewards and staff can insert or update one (a blocked INSERT raises InsufficientPrivilege, a blocked UPDATE silently changes no row), and every role in the org plus staff may upload to the org's document vault.

test_agent_rls.py proves the Ask agent's validated SQL runs as the caller through agent_caller and PsycopgExecutor: a member sees its own org's private document but not another org's or a staff-only funder_activity row, a signed-in user with no organisation and a run with no caller (anon) see no private rows, the connection returns to the pool as owner with claims cleared, and every catalogued column is SELECT-able by authenticated. Unlike test_rls.py it commits marker-tagged rows and deletes them in a finally block.

test_proposals_work.py pins work.apply as the single proposal write path: paths outside the allowed shapes raise BadChange, a batch is atomic, section changes need the rev they were read at and a stale one raises StaleSection naming the current text and who changed it, rev rises once per save per section, every change is logged with who/via/run_id/path/from/to/facts/reason, stage moves back by patch and forward only with advance, and the summary is recomputed.

test_proposal_agent.py unit-tests (with no database) who may run the proposal chat via proposal_chat_access (admins and stewards get their own thread proposal-<id>-<user>; members get 403; strangers and foreign or malformed threads get 404; two editors never share a chat), that advance_step refuses a reader before repo.save is reached, what the stable and live context blocks contain, that only Anthropic gets the cache breakpoint, and that the built agent exposes exactly ten tools including read_file and no other filesystem tool.

The remaining proposal tests are DB-free rule tests that pin code-enforced safeguards: trace check, fact origin and question rules, suggest_edit outcomes, polish refusing any changed figure/year/place/name/gap, reader tool sets (file reader, funder reader, and a public researcher that reads the web and no file and is not built without a search key), a PublicGuard that refuses searches naming the organisation, per-file isolation with a busy lock and stale limit, and correction propagation; they monkeypatch repository functions and context rather than touching a pool.

ci.yml runs on every pull request and every push to master with read-only contents permission (id-token write only on jobs that upload coverage) and four jobs: backend-lint (ruff check), backend-unit (pytest -m "not integration" with coverage), backend-integration (a pgvector pg17 service on port 5433 that is baselined from db/init, migrated and seeded before pytest -m integration, with skips listed via -rs and two dump-restore tests deselected) and frontend (lint, tsc --noEmit, npm run coverage with a Codecov upload, then build). It deploys nothing.

Nothing deploys automatically: deploy.yml is triggered only by workflow_dispatch (run by hand) and is the only workflow that deploys, with Git-integration deploys turned off; CI and dependency review never deploy.

dependency-review.yml runs on pull requests with actions/dependency-review-action, failing a PR whose lockfile changes add a package with a high or critical advisory and commenting in the PR only on failure; it checks only what the PR changes.

CI uploads three coverage reports per commit to Codecov (backend unit and backend integration coverage.xml under separate flags, and the frontend lcov.info under flag frontend) using OIDC, tokenless for forks. codecov.yml turns the global project and patch statuses off and gates the backend and frontend components separately, each with a 75% project floor, a drop rule failing a PR that lowers coverage by more than 1% from the base commit, and a 75% patch check; it remaps report paths to backend/ and frontend/ and carries flags forward. Backend measurement is configured in backend/pyproject.toml (source app, branch coverage, relative files).

With Langfuse keys set, the selected Ask eval cases run once as a dataset experiment on ask-golden named branch-sha under the eval environment, with golden.jsonl as source of truth and the dataset a copy upserted by case id; cases run one at a time because the agent's tools share one module-level pool; run stats (tool calls, tokens, large-result reads) are counted from messages, call and large-read budgets fail a case, while seconds and token counts are only reported; without keys the cases run as an untraced loop.

test_import_calls.py is a DB-free, model-free unit test of the Import eval's tool-call accounting: a scripted supervisor and researcher show ToolCalls counts a subagent's call under both the bare tool name and agent.tool, and call_failures fails only calls over their max_calls budget (0 forbids a tool, no budget never fails).

test_agent_middleware.py pins that clearing old tool results (clear_old_tool_results in app/agentkit/middleware.py) keeps the prompt prefix cache-stable: nothing is cleared below the trigger, the cleared set moves at most once per clear step, what is sent stays under the trigger however long the turn, the latest results and compare_fit results are kept, and failed db_profile_column calls count toward Ask's SQL retry budget like db_query ones.

test_ask_budgets.py pins Ask's code-level limits: compare_fit refuses repeated arguments and a fourth call per question (a new question resets), model_call_cap ends the turn with a capped message, and the built Ask stack has a model fallback on the research tier (omitted when tiers are one model), summarisation on the utility tier, and a CompareFitBudget, with the cap's exit still reaching an after_agent hook or end.

test_tool_errors.py pins that a raising tool answers the model with an error ToolMessage carrying only the tool name and exception type (no message text, so secrets do not leak) while GraphInterrupt still pauses, and that exactly one ToolErrorMiddleware is present on Ask, on Import and each of its four subagents, and on the Pitch agent and its readers (three stacks when built without a search key).

The eval harness runs the Ask agent as the staff dev user and also resets caveats_given and sets chat_user_id to the dev user, because compare_fit refuses an unset chat user as someone who may not run a match.

test_audit.py pins the post-answer SQL audit: it audits only the current turn (a new human message resets it), reads SQL from the db_query artifact or the 'executed:' text line, makes no model call when disabled, when no SQL ran, or when no answer exists, accepts ok/warn verdicts (JSON wrapped in prose is read; warn without a caveat becomes ok), and fails open (returns None) on model errors, unresolvable models, unparseable replies or malformed JSON; an appended CAVEAT_PREFIX message is not mistaken for the answer.

test_proposal_agent.py pins the Pitch agent's nothing_to_answer guard: a run whose history ends on an assistant reply ends without calling the model, a new human message is answered, a pending tool call is not an answer, and the guard is in the Pitch agent's main middleware stack.

The frontend Vitest suite has two projects: *.test.ts run in node for pure modules and *.test.tsx run in jsdom with tests/setup.ts, which mocks next/navigation (mutable pathname and search), mocks next/link, stubs IntersectionObserver and cleans up and resets mocks after each test; a test that renders a component must therefore be .tsx.

Frontend coverage uses the v8 provider and includes every file under lib, features and components regardless of whether a test imports it (excluding tests, __tests__ and .d.ts), so the figure is honest; CI runs npm run coverage and uploads lcov.info, while the failing thresholds live in codecov.yml's frontend component (75% floor, 1% drop, 75% patch) rather than in the Vitest config.

test_architecture.py enforces the code-boundary rules from CLAUDE.md over the source with ast and no database: only an agent builder may import from tools/ (R1); function-level imports are allowed only on cold-start paths or in a shrink-only CYCLES set (R2); ask, ingest and proposals import each other only through a listed shared set and importing app.main must not load deepagents or langchain (R3); no app file exceeds 800 lines except the catalog and finding_types (R4); every top-level function or class has a caller outside tests (R6).

The test_cov_*.py family exists to cover code the behaviour suites do not reach so Codecov floors and patch checks hold: they use hand-built state, fakes and monkeypatched repositories, share cov_ingest_fakes.py (a scripted ScriptConn pool and running_as scope helper) for Import tool tests, and only a subset (migration runner, matcher, promotion, repositories, writer, reshelve/undo) are marked integration and run in the database job.

Storage tests pin the file-trust boundary against httpx.MockTransport: storage is enabled only when both supabase_url and supabase_service_key are set, a disabled client makes no request, failures are return values rather than exceptions, owned_split trusts a path only inside the row's own folder (org-vault/<exact org id>, staff-sources only for non-public rows with no org), and with storage_bucket_suffix every call names the suffixed bucket while rows keep the plain name, with the suffix dropped when the database is the storage project's own.

The bucket migration 0020 is checked at file level (both buckets created and private, guarded by pg_namespace for plain Postgres, idempotent via ON CONFLICT) and the vault bucket's allowed MIME types in migration 0055 must equal storage.VAULT_TYPES.

Doc Vault route tests (via client_for with monkeypatched repo and storage) pin that upload URLs are minted only for members with a key leading with the org id, unreadable types are 415 before any URL, non-members and unknown orgs both get 403, confirm refuses another org's folder, the archive bucket, missing objects, already-recorded paths (409, never read or removed) and files whose bytes do not match their extension (object removed, 415), a file unreadable back gets 503 with no row, downloads of private or out-of-folder rows are 404, and delete is staff-only with DocumentInUse->409, FileNotRemoved->502, RowNotRemoved->500.

Integration classes in test_vault.py prove the SQL the route tests monkeypatch: org_id_for_member lets a member read and write, a steward read but not write, an outsider nothing and staff write without membership; delete_vault_upload removes row and file together but refuses (before touching the file) documents with chunks or used by a proposal as draft, template or budget, and deletes only private vault_upload rows. They use _PoolOf from test_storage.py to run repositories inside the rolled-back fixture transaction.

test_deleted_documents.py (integration) pins that every DELETE on documents writes the whole old row as JSON into deleted_documents regardless of who deletes it, and that a delete refused by the repository (FileNotRemoved) logs nothing.

test_proposal_form.py pins filling a funder's own form in code: form.check keeps the form's order, numbers and groups and assigns T-codes; PDFs go to the model as document blocks, Word as text and other types raise Unreadable; fill.check refuses an added or changed figure or an over-limit answer but allows cuts and new gaps; fill.resolve gives each heading answered/add/you_fill, turns refused answers into logged [Add:] marks, always leaves tables for the person, drops skipped and second-phase headings, and trims over-limit answers at sentence or semicolon boundaries; form.read sends at most 100 pages and says why an unusable form is refused.

test_proposal_regex_linear.py is a performance guard: the proposal gap, amount, extract and drop_cites regexes that CodeQL flagged as polynomial must finish a 50,000-character hostile input in under a second, and the rewritten functions must match the old regexes on realistic text.

test_proposal_facts.py pins the fact list's code-only rules: reliability tier by origin (registry and vault green, web and derived amber, you_said said, unknown origin raises), when a question is warranted (missing element, disagreement between equally strong sources, only the organisation's call on an amount) and the ask gate that refuses a gap open with a teammate.

lib/__tests__/copilotkit-route.test.ts calls the real CopilotKit route handlers with no cookie or Authorization and requires /info to return 200 while the runtime's thread-store routes (GET /threads, /threads/<id>/events, /threads/<id>/messages, POST /threads/clear) return 404, because allowRoute in lib/copilotkit-access.ts serves only info and the agent run/connect/stop/suggest methods and throws a 404 Response otherwise (chat history comes from the backend's /api/threads).

Routers take PoolDep, which builds a CallerPool over Depends(get_pool), so the single get_pool override in conftest.make_app covers every router; the recording_pool fixture (RecordingPool) is the DB-free way to test repository SQL: it answers each query with the next scripted row list, records (sql, params) in calls, and fails on any unscripted extra query.

test_paging.py pins repositories/paging.fetch_page without a database: it appends LIMIT/OFFSET and binds limit and offset, reads the total from the first row in one query, returns total 0 for an empty first page without a second query, runs one count(*) subquery with the original params when a page is past the end, and raises ValueError before any query unless the SQL ends in an outermost ORDER BY whose last key is id (rejecting no tie-breaker, a trailing semicolon, its own LIMIT, a trailing comment, or an ORDER BY only in a subquery); a parametrized test applies that guard to each of the ten paged list functions so every list must sort on a unique id.

Per-resource unit tests check that list_rfps, list_scores and list_documents pass their filters and limit/offset through fetch_page (asserted via recording_pool params), and route tests assert the {items, total, limit, offset} envelope, with GET /api/scores answering 422 rather than clamping an out-of-range limit and GET /api/registry refusing limit 0 or 101 and a negative offset.

test_registry.py unit-tests the GET /api/registry route: query parameters map to a Filters value (type=cso becomes kind org, unknown types become all), research counts are read only for the page's rows and not at all for an empty page, a failing research read leaves the page up, and a row's themes lead with the tags most of its programmes carry, leaving lenses out; test_registry_filters.py requires the backend NORTH_EAST list to equal the list in frontend/features/registry/rows.ts.

test_registry_sql.py is an integration test of registry_page_sql against Postgres in the rolled-back db fixture: CSOs sort before funders each A to Z ignoring case, each filter applies (registrations to CSOs only, funder type and approach to funders only), search reads aliases, programmes and states, total counts every match, counts and facets are computed only for the first page (a later page returns empty ones and its plan cuts the facet counting), and registrations are read through the owner pool for the page's orgs only.

ListPage.test.tsx pins the shared list hooks and components: usePagedList (offset paging) loads offset 0 then the next offset, uses a server-rendered first page without refetching, restarts and drops stale answers when its key changes, de-duplicates rows shifted between pages while counting fetched, and clears total and last when a new key's first page fails; useCursorList follows next_cursor without repeats and drops answers for a stale key; ListMore offers at most a page more, shows 'End of the list', and triggers near the end only after a scroll.

RegistryClient.test.tsx mocks fetchRegistryPage and renders with a server-shaped first page: it makes no request on first render, asks the server once typing pauses or a dropdown is picked (with limit 25 and the current text), asks once when a search is cleared with the filters, requests offset 25 for the next batch while keeping the first page's counts and facet options, writes filter changes to the address as a replace dropping defaults, and shows only the active bucket's own filters.
